subject: Dedicated reservation questionnaire and fallback plan

Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire (OpticAI RFI)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. Attached is the questionnaire that procurement asked us to submit as part of the RFP — most focused on dedicated/reserved capacity (GPU types, throughput targets per model class, reservation phasing and fallback options). High-level asks:

- Confirm supported GPU families (A100, H100, L4 equivalence) and recommended mix for a 2M monthly token footprint at 99th %-ile tail latency targets.
- Provide throughput (tokens/sec) estimates for medium-sequence chat and long-generation workloads for each SKU.
- Describe reservation phasing: pilot -> 50% commit -> full commit, and what burst or fallback options exist.
- Any contractual constraints (SLA carveouts, eviction rules) and time-to-scale for burst capacity.

I attached the procurement spreadsheet (OpticAI_RFI_Dedicated_Questions.xlsx). Can you please return a filled sheet or a short summary by EOD Tuesday? We are on a tight cadence for evaluation.

Regards,
Samira
Head of Procurement, OpticAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire (OpticAI RFI)

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clear list. I started a short summary and attached a two-page response plus a compact GPU throughput CSV to help map your estimated workload to SKU choices. Quick notes up front:

- Supported GPU families: H100 (8x, 16GB/80GB variants), A100 (40GB/80GB), and our inference-optimized L4 equivalents for cost-sensitive low-latency tasks. We recommend a blended pool for mixed workloads.
- For your 2M tokens/month example, our suggested starting pool is: 4x H100-equivalent slots + 8x A100-equivalent slots with an L4 cache tier for short chat state.
- Burst: we support burst capacity up to 2.5x committed throughput for short periods (pre-agreed); automatic routing to hosted pool is available as fallback when local capacity is saturated.
- SLA and eviction: we provide reservation SLAs for throughput and median latency; 99th percentile tail latency is covered in the Dedicated SLO addendum, but tail slots may be preempted under extreme overload with a 15-minute notification window unless you opt into our higher-priority lane.

I attached: Redwood_RFI_Response_Summary.pdf and gpu_throughput_table.csv. Ben — looped you for any commercial carveouts. If you can share a representative token distribution (sequence length histogram + concurrency), we can replace the heuristic numbers with measured projection.

Next step: I can pull together a phased commitment plan (pilot -> half commit -> full) and a simple Mutual Action Plan doc. Would Tuesday EOD work?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

Forwarding the OpticAI RFI; they want a filled sheet by EOD Tuesday (their timezone). I drafted a short summary for Samira but we need:

1) Marcus: please confirm the per-SKU throughput for the model classes below (tokens/sec for medium chat (seq=128) and long generation (seq=2048)) and attach the workbook you used to compute these.
2) Ben: pricing/commitment tiers and the guardrails on burst > 2x - are standbys automatically billed, or do we require pre-approval? Need the commercial language we can send to procurement.
3) Grace: confirm operational lead time to add 10 H100-equivalent slots in a dedicated pool and the steps for hosted fallback routing (networking, latency delta).

I want to keep the external reply concise — just numbers and a phased proposal. Hit reply-all with your inputs by EOD so I can consolidate.

-Kim
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated capacity questionnaire (internal: OpticAI RFI)

Kim,

See numbers below (rounded and conservative):

- H100-equivalent (80GB): medium chat (seq=128): ~1,200 tokens/sec; long-gen (seq=2048): ~160 tokens/sec.
- A100-equivalent (80GB): medium chat: ~850 tokens/sec; long-gen: ~110 tokens/sec.
- L4 class: medium chat: ~2200 tokens/sec (small batch, short seq); long-gen: ~N/A (not recommended for >1024).

Recommended pool for 2M tokens/month (99th pct tail target 600ms):
- Pilot (30 days): 2x H100 + 4x A100 + L4 cache tier (2 nodes).
- Phase 2 (50% commit): 4x H100 + 6x A100 + L4 cache tier (4 nodes).
- Full commit (100%): 6x H100 + 10x A100 with autoscale headroom and reserved L4 cache.

Burst/fallback: we can promise 2.5x burst for up to 72 hours with pre-negotiated credit allowances. After that, fallback to hosted pool with cross-region routing (expected latency increase 25-40ms RTT).

I uploaded the spreadsheet draft as gpu_mix_recommendation.xlsx (link in internal drive). If OpticAI can confirm pct of short chats vs long-gen and concurrency profiles we can tighten numbers.

-Marcus
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire (OpticAI RFI)

Hi Samira / Ethan —

Thanks for the RFI. Please find a consolidated reply below and attached short workbook for your procurement team. Key points up front:

- Supported SKUs and recommended mix: H100-equivalent (primary for large seq), A100-equivalent (balanced), L4 cache tier (short, high-req throughput). See attached table for tokens/sec per SKU.

- Throughput estimates (examples): H100: 1,200 t/s (seq=128), 160 t/s (seq=2048). A100: 850 t/s / 110 t/s. L4: 2,200 t/s (short seq). These are conservative per-slot expectations to give headroom.

- Phased reservation plan (mutual action plan):
  * Pilot (30 days): 2x H100 + 4x A100 + L4 cache (2) — validate tail latency and cache hit rates.
  * Phase 2 (50% commit): 4x H100 + 6x A100 + L4 (4) — run steady-state traffic for 60 days.
  * Full (100% commit): 6x H100 + 10x A100 with automatic autoscale headroom and agreed burst credits.

- Burst and fallback: Up to 2.5x burst for short windows (72 hours) via reserved credit pool. If sustained beyond agreed burst, requests route to Redwood hosted pool (transparent fallback) with an expected median latency increase of 25–40ms; we provide monitoring and automatic retries. You can opt into a High-Priority lane (paid) to avoid fallback.

- SLA language highlights: Dedicated reservation covers committed throughput and median latency. 99th pct tail latency is included in SLO monitoring; we offer an addendum with deeper guarantees for an additional commitment. Eviction: preemption only under extreme platform-wide events; otherwise slice isolation is enforced.

Next steps:
- Can you share a representative token-length histogram and concurrency profile (simple CSV) so we can run the workbook and produce a final price/slot recommendation?
- Proposed meeting to review the workbook: Wed 11/24 10:00am PT or Thu 11/25 2:00pm PT — which works?

I've attached the short summary (Redwood_RFI_Response_Summary.pdf) and the throughput table (gpu_throughput_table.csv). Ben will follow up on commercial terms and credit/burst wording right after.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
